Dosage information

Ozempic dosage

The Ozempic label starts the weekly injection at 0.25 mg for 4 weeks, then 0.5 mg.1 A prescriber may raise it to 1 mg and then 2 mg, the maximum, each after at least 4 weeks.1 The Ozempic pill runs from 1.5 mg to 9 mg daily.2 These are label facts, not advice for any person.

This page summarizes published sources for information only. It is not medical advice and does not tell anyone to use a product. Questions about your own health belong with a licensed clinician. For questions about an order or a product, contact us.

Ozempic dosage on the label

This is the label's schedule for the weekly injection in adults with type 2 diabetes.1

Step Weekly dose When
Start1 0.25 mg Weeks 1 to 4; an initiation dose, not a maintenance dose
First increase1 0.5 mg From week 5
Possible increase1 1 mg After at least 4 weeks on 0.5 mg, if more blood sugar control is needed
Possible increase1 2 mg (maximum) After at least 4 weeks on 1 mg, if more blood sugar control is needed

Maintenance for blood sugar control is 0.5 mg, 1 mg or 2 mg once a week.1 For adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, the label's maintenance dose is 1 mg once a week, reached after at least 4 weeks on 0.5 mg.1 Whether to raise the dose, and when, is the prescriber's decision; the label ties each increase to a need for more blood sugar control.1 The 2 mg once-weekly dose joined the label on March 28, 2022.3

Why the dose starts low

The label gives one reason for the slow climb: it lowers the risk of stomach and gut side effects, which in the trials clustered in the dose-increase period.1 Rates by dose are on the Ozempic side effects page.

Which pen gives which dose

Each multi-dose pen holds 3 mL of solution and is for one patient only.1

Pen or syringe Concentration Doses it gives
2 mg/3 mL pen1 0.68 mg/mL 0.25 mg or 0.5 mg: 4 doses of 0.25 mg and 2 of 0.5 mg, or 4 doses of 0.5 mg
4 mg/3 mL pen1 1.34 mg/mL 4 doses of 1 mg
8 mg/3 mL pen1 2.68 mg/mL 4 doses of 2 mg
Single-dose prefilled syringe1 0.25, 0.5 or 1 mg in 0.5 mL One complete dose per syringe

FDA lists an older 2 mg/1.5 mL pen (1.34 mg/mL) as discontinued.3 An opened pen is thrown away 56 days after first use, even if medicine is left.1

Timing and changing the injection day

Doses fall on the same day each week, at any time of day, with or without meals.1 The day can be moved as long as at least 2 days (more than 48 hours) separate two doses.1

Ozempic pill dosage

The tablets have their own schedule, taken once a day by mouth.2

Days Daily dose
1 to 302 1.5 mg, a starter dose that does not control blood sugar
31 to 602 4 mg
From day 612 4 mg or 9 mg

The label says Ozempic tablets and Rybelsus tablets (3, 7 and 14 mg) are not interchangeable milligram for milligram.2 People on the 0.5 mg weekly injection may switch: one week after the last 0.5 mg injection, the label starts 4 mg or 9 mg Ozempic tablets, or 7 mg or 14 mg Rybelsus, once a day.2

Other medicines, kidneys and liver

When Ozempic is started, the label says to consider lowering the dose of insulin or of an insulin secretagogue, such as a sulfonylurea, taken with it, to reduce the risk of low blood sugar.1 Ozempic delays stomach emptying, which could change how other oral medicines are absorbed; trials did not show a clinically relevant effect, but the label advises caution.1 No dose change is recommended for kidney or liver impairment.1

Doses are in milligrams, not units

FDA-approved semaglutide injections are dosed in milligrams, at standard concentrations,4 and Ozempic comes in prefilled pens and syringes.1 FDA has received adverse event reports, some needing hospital care, after dosing errors with compounded semaglutide drawn from multi-dose vials.4 In most of these reports, patients drew more than the prescribed amount and gave themselves 5 to 20 times more than the intended dose.4

FDA says confusion between milliliters, milligrams and syringe 'units' may have contributed.4 In several reports, people told to draw 5 units (0.05 mL) on a U-100 insulin syringe drew 50 units (0.5 mL), ten times the intended amount.4 Some prescribers also miscalculated when converting milligrams to units or milliliters, and their patients took 5 to 10 times more than the intended dose.4 FDA notes that overdose effects include severe nausea, severe vomiting and severe low blood sugar, and that semaglutide's half-life of about one week can mean a long period of observation and treatment.4

Why this is not advice for you

These figures are the label schedule for the FDA-approved product.1 The prescriber sets the starting point, each increase and the maintenance dose for each person.1 The label numbers belong to the approved product alone: FDA says compounded GLP-1 drugs are not FDA approved or reviewed for safety, effectiveness or quality, and that semaglutide sold 'for research purposes' is an unapproved drug of unknown quality.5

Frequently asked questions

How much Ozempic is needed per month?

Each maintenance pen holds 4 weekly doses, about a month of injections: the 4 mg/3 mL pen gives four 1 mg doses and the 8 mg/3 mL pen four 2 mg doses, while the 2 mg/3 mL pen covers the 0.25 mg and 0.5 mg steps.1 Single-dose prefilled syringes come 4 to a carton.1 How much any one person uses depends on the dose their prescriber sets.

How is Ozempic normally prescribed?

The label covers adults with type 2 diabetes, alongside diet and exercise.1 Treatment starts at 0.25 mg injected under the skin once a week for 4 weeks, an initiation dose rather than a maintenance dose, and then moves to 0.5 mg.1 The prescriber may later raise it to 1 mg or 2 mg if more blood sugar control is needed, or choose the once-daily Ozempic tablets, which follow their own schedule.12

What happens if you miss a dose of Ozempic?

The label says to take a missed weekly dose as soon as possible within 5 days.1 If more than 5 days have passed, the missed dose is skipped and the next one is taken on the usual day.1 The window differs between drugs in the class: a missed dose of Mounjaro, a weekly tirzepatide injection, may be taken within 4 days.7

What is the highest dose of Ozempic?

The maximum on the injection label is 2 mg once a week, reached only after at least 4 weeks at 1 mg.1 For the Ozempic pill, the highest daily strength is 9 mg.2 Wegovy, which contains the same semaglutide, has a usual maintenance dose of 2.4 mg weekly and can go up to 7.2 mg, and its label says not to use it with other semaglutide products.6
